subject: VPC: Phased minor patch, sentinel & rollback plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, devops@edgecloud.com; ops@acme.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: VPC: Phased minor patch, sentinel & rollback plan

Team / partners —

Proposed plan for the December minor patch across our Private (VPC) customers — this thread captures schedule, version pinning, maintenance windows, and explicit rollback triggers. Goal: ship v2.4.2 (bugfix, networking and KV-cache regression fix) with minimal customer impact and clear rollback guardrails.

High-level summary:
- Target image: redwood-inference-server:v2.4.2 (patch from v2.4.1).
- Why: connection drop under high concurrent prefix-cache warmups (observed in canary).
- Patch scope: runtime binary + networking helper (iptables rules hygiene) + restart ordering to preserve KV cache warmup.
- Version pinning: customers on v2.4.x will be offered a phased opt-in. For Dedicated/Private, we will push as a managed maintenance unless customer pins exact minor (option in console).

Proposed maintenance windows (phased):
1) Preflight window (non-customer-impact): Dec 15 02:00-05:00 UTC — run preflight validation on 10% of nodes (internal only).
2) Canary phase: Dec 16 00:00-06:00 UTC — 5% of customer VPCs (prefer low-TPS customers: Acme Financial agreed to be canary).
3) Phased rollout: Dec 17-20 00:00-08:00 UTC each day — incremental batches (10 -> 25 -> 50%).
4) Full completion: by Dec 21 23:59 UTC.

Rollback & gating rules (summary):
- Automated rollback trigger if 5xx rate increases >0.75% above baseline for 15 minutes OR median p99 tail latency regresses >25% for 10 minutes.
- Manual rollback if KV cache hit rate drops >10% and application error rate increases.
- Rollback process documented in rollback-playbook.md (attached).

Networking considerations:
- Connectivity pre-check: ensure BGP route propagation and VPC peering integrity (EdgeCloud to run preflight).
- Temporary iptables change required; will apply with staged rule precedence to avoid transient blackholes.
- Port 7000/7001 ephemeral changes noted in checklist (vpc-preflight-checklist.pdf).

Attachments: canary-matrix.xlsx, rollback-playbook.md, vpc-preflight-checklist.pdf (links below).

Ask: please confirm availability for the proposed windows and call out any customer-specific constraints. If we get sign-off by EOD Thu (Dec 10), we will lock schedule and run preflight automation.

--
Irene Choi
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: devops@edgecloud.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC: Phased minor patch, sentinel & rollback plan

Thanks Irene — useful summary. A couple quick technical clarifications from runtime/ops: 

1) Canary KPIs we should track (continuous):
   - 5xx rate (per-routing-key), per-tenant latency p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, active connection churn.
2) Cache warmup: the new ordering preserves existing in-memory KV cache on restart when possible; however, we will still see a transient cold-hit window. Can we schedule a warmup-only job post-deploy to pre-populate frequent prefixes? I put a note in the canary-matrix.
3) Network rule change: can we do a staged Netfilter insertion with complementing DNAT fallback to avoid blackholing? I recommend a 30s delayed activation after validation.

One ask: add a smoke-test step that runs a synthetic multi-tenant workload for 20 minutes post-upgrade and reports through our trace pipeline. If smoke fails, automatic halt and rollback.

I'll attach a short checklist snippet into the Drive folder.

- Dev
Senior Site Reliability Engineer

From: EdgeCloud Partners <devops@edgecloud.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC: Phased minor patch, sentinel & rollback plan

Hi Irene / team —

EdgeCloud can support the proposed windows. A few items on our side: 
- We will run BGP and route-refresh tests 24 hours before each phased rollout; expect brief route reconvergence windows (we'll surface if >60s).
- We recommend the canary run on subnets with no overlapping customer IPs to minimize blast radius; Acme Financial offered their dev VPC as candidate.
- We will pre-stage the iptables rules and run a dry-run apply on a subset of nodes (no traffic) to validate rule syntax and NETLINK interactions.

Two requests:
1) Provide the exact iptables rule diffs as a Gist or attachment so our automation can pre-validate.
2) Confirm who is the escalation contact (pager) during each window; we need a single on-call name per 6-hour window.

Regards,
Maya (EdgeCloud Partner Ops)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: devops@edgecloud.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC: Phased minor patch, sentinel & rollback plan

Good plan. Quick operational notes from CS & reliability: 

- Sentinel & automation: we should bind the smoke-test pass/fail to an automated gate in our rollout pipeline (INF-deploy). If the smoke fails, the pipeline should: 1) mark the batch FAILED, 2) trigger rollback as per rollback-playbook.md, and 3) notify stakeholders via PagerDuty and Slack channel #private-upgrades.
- Customer comms: prepare a short mail to customers in the affected batches 48 hours before their window; avoid detailed technicals but include exact maintenance start/expected duration and opt-out instructions to pin versions.
- SLA exceptions: if we cross SLO during an upgrade, open an incident and route to Incident Response. We should pre-authorize a 60-minute maintenance grace for transient blips in the canary (document in Jira INF-9724).

For on-call coverage: I will volunteer Evelyn-Hart as primary for the preflight and canary; Dev, please propose the secondary for the 00:00-06:00 UTC slot.

Evelyn
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: devops@edgecloud.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC: Phased minor patch, sentinel & rollback plan

Adding the rollback runbook excerpt and canary gating matrix. Quoting the key steps below (full runbook attached as rollback-playbook.md):

> Rollback runbook (summary):
> 1) Halt new batch rollouts immediately (INF-deploy pause).
> 2) For affected nodes, push redwood-inference-server:v2.4.1 and restart in reverse-order of the upgrade batches to minimize KV cache thrash.
> 3) If reverse-order rollback does not stabilize within 20 minutes, execute network-level fallback: remove new iptables rules and insert prior rule set (automated by EdgeCloud pre-staged apply).
> 4) If network fallback still fails, failover traffic to warm standby region for affected tenants (requires approval from on-call lead).

Canary gating matrix (from canary-matrix.xlsx):
- Batch size 5% (canary): require 0.5% max increase in 5xx and <15% drop in KV hit-rate over baseline for 30m window.
- Batch size 10%: require <0.75% 5xx delta and <10% KV drop for 30m.
- Subsequent batches: progressively allow 1% 5xx delta as long as p99 < baseline*1.25.

Notes: ensure we capture traces with tenant tag and route them to the canary dashboard. Also, add an explicit step to drain long-lived connections on hosts prior to restart (graceful SIGTERM + 90s drain).

- Karthik
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

- Canary (Acme dev VPC): 2026-12-16 00:00-06:00 UTC.
- Rollout: 2026-12-17 through 2026-12-20 00:00-08:00 UTC daily windows.

Primary contacts and on-call:

- Runtime/rollback lead: Karthik Iyer (pager: +1-555-0202)

I will create the Jira ticket and update INF-9724 with the schedule and links. Thank you all for the quick turn-around.

Irene
